subject: Appeal: temporary SLA carve-out for filtering-triggered structured-output failures
messages:
From: Carlos Mendes <carlos.mendes@finsecure.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: security-ops@finsecure.com
Date: Fri, 15 Jan 2027 16:27:00 -0800
Subject: Structured output failures caused by filtering — request for temporary SLA carve-out

Hi Sofia,

We started a progressive rollout of Redwood's structured-output option last week and have seen a spike in requests that are being rejected by the content filter. The filter is flagging predicates in legitimate finance templates (IBAN-like strings, account IDs) and Redwood is returning structured-output errors rather than generated responses. This impacts our reconciliation workflow; outages are intermittent but measurable.

I've attached a sample snapshot and the raw request logs for the windows where we saw failures. At a high level: 12% of structured-output calls in the last 48 hours returned a filter-triggered error, and our downstream worker retries cause a 2x latency amplification for affected jobs.

Given the operational impact and our SLA expectations, we'd like to request a temporary carve-out or credit for filter-caused structured-output failures while we work with your team on a mitigation plan. Specifically: 1) a temporary adjustment of the SLA attribution so these failures don't count against uptime/latency SLOs, and 2) a short-term runbook/whitelist path to avoid blocking our reconciliation flow.

Can we set up a triage call early next week? We can share the internal traces and sample payloads.

Thanks,
Carlos Mendes
Head of Reliability, FinSecure

Attachments: filter_failures_snapshot_20270115.json (sample requests), request_logs_20270115-01.zip (500KB)

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Mendes <carlos.mendes@finsecure.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 09:11:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Structured output failures caused by filtering — request for temporary SLA carve-out

Hi Carlos — thanks for the detailed note and the logs. I'm really sorry you're seeing this during the rollout.

Quick answers:
- We can absolutely prioritize a technical triage. Neha (CS) and Rishi (Infra) are looped in.
- For SLA implications, we typically classify filter blocks as "policy-induced" failures and they are not always eligible for uptime credits unless we can demonstrate a service regression. That said, we have an internal process for conditional carve-outs when a customer provides reproducible failure patterns and we deploy mitigations (whitelists, model routing changes, or exception rules).

Proposed next steps:
1) Triage call Tuesday 2027-01-19 10:00 PT — Rishi to review logs and propose mitigation options.
2) Customer provides the most sensitive examples and any transformations you apply to payloads (you already attached some good ones).
3) Redwood delivers a mitigation plan and a temporary attribution decision within 48 hours of the triage call — if we confirm a regressional filtering behavior, we'll scope a provisional SLA carve-out and credits.

I've attached an intake checklist to help structure the call. Please confirm the Tuesday slot or suggest alternatives.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | Developer-first inference

Attachment: intake_checklist_sla_triage.pdf (stub)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Jan 2027 08:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Internal: quick run-through before FinSecure triage (notes)

Internal notes (internal recipients only) — please keep this thread internal.

Summary of artifacts Carlos provided: snapshot with 47 sample requests, policy labels showing high-confidence matches on numeric sequences and tokenized IBAN-like fragments, and request-level latency traces.

Initial hypotheses: 
- This looks like the conservative policy threshold on the content-filter model is producing false positives for their financial templates.
- The structured-output code path currently treats filter-triggered rejections as an immediate failure (400-style error), which then bubbles to the client without an automatic fallback. For many customers we prefer a graceful degradation (partial output or model variant fallback) to avoid systemic throughput amplification.

Suggested short-term mitigations for triage call:
1) Exception rule scoped to FinSecure's production prefix for 72 hours (temporary whitelist).
2) Route structured-output calls to a lower-sensitivity variant of the filter for this customer only.
3) Instrument a KV-cache bypass but keep a tokenized audit trail for compliance.

SLA attribution guidance draft (for Neha/Legal): if we deploy mitigation within 48 hours and confirm the root cause is conservative filter thresholds (not customer payload abuse), propose marking those incidents as "filter-attribution — mitigation applied" and exclude them from uptime SLO penalties for the affected window. Credits would be evaluated proportionally to request volume impacted.

Open questions for the call: do we need a signed addendum to change the SLA attribution for the temporary period? (Legal may require minimal change to the order form.)

Rishi
Staff Engineer, Inference Runtime

Attachment: rishi_triage_notes_20270119.md (internal stub)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Mendes <carlos.mendes@finsecure.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 20 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Structured output failures caused by filtering — request for temporary SLA carve-out

Hi Carlos — great triage call this morning, thank you for walking us through the traces. Per Rishi's analysis, we're prepared to move forward with a two-week mitigation window:

1) Immediate: 72-hour scoped exception rule applied to your production prefix at 11:00 PT today.
2) Short-term: route structured-output calls for your account to the lower-sensitivity filter variant for 14 days while our policy team refines thresholds.
3) SLA attribution: Redwood will not count filter-triggered structured-output rejections against your uptime SLO for the period starting at the time the exception is applied. We'll calculate any credit proportionally and present it in a follow-up note within 5 business days.

Action items for FinSecure: please confirm you accept the scoped exception and temporary routing. Also confirm whether you need a signed 1-page addendum or if an email acknowledgment is sufficient for your procurement team.

I'll coordinate with Legal and Billing on the credit calculation and any minimal paperwork. Thanks for your partnership on this — we'll monitor closely and share daily status updates to the drive link.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
